other_fabrications.sentence: Social worker Priya Nair conducted a needs assessment visit on Monday following a referral from the hospital after Margaret Doyle's discharge.
other_fabrications.why: Monday was the earlier phone call (L0001); the day of the visit is not stated.

other_fabrications.sentence: Margaret Doyle lives in a home with heating that she feels is too cold for the current season.
other_fabrications.why: She has the heating on although she thinks she shouldn't at this time of year, because she feels the cold (L0004); she does not say the heating is inadequate.

other_fabrications.sentence: Margaret Doyle stated she is interested in the assessment and has no objection to it.
other_fabrications.why: The cited 'Go on then. Interested. Put it down.' (L0176) is her agreeing to be noted as interested in a wrist-worn alarm, not about the assessment.

other_fabrications.sentence: Margaret Doyle stated she would not sell the house because she would not know where her dog 'Biscuit' would go or where Frank's roses would go.
Margaret Doyle stated Kevin usually contributes money ('tuppence') to the household expenses.
other_fabrications.why: 'He'll want to put his tuppence in' (L0050) means he will give his opinion; nothing about money.

other_fabrications.sentence: Kevin Doyle instructed the social worker to see the person again on the fifteenth.
other_fabrications.why: Priya proposed the review visit on Tuesday 15 April (L0656); Kevin only said he would try to be there (L0659, L0679).

notes: Detailed on the fall, falls history, continence, cooking and weight, but stops around the first third of the visit: nothing on meds, family, mood, Jordan, finances or most actions. Several misreadings of idioms and context (tuppence, heating, 'dog' Biscuit).
